executiveSummary: Surveillance data spanning October 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent public health threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas Region represents the highest-priority concern given its pandemic potential and BSL-3 select agent status, with two separate PAHO updates indicating sustained circulation. Additional elevated concerns include Mpox (BSL-3 select agent) circulating in the Americas, Yellow Fever activity, and a Dengue surge in the Americas. European ECDC weekly threat reports across Weeks 16-20 of 2026 suggest ongoing communicable disease monitoring activity across the EU/EEA region.
bottomLine: Concurrent H5N1 avian influenza and Mpox activity in the Americas, both involving BSL-3 select agents, represent the most critical biosecurity concerns requiring immediate enhanced surveillance and response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained H5N1 activity
BSL-3 select agent with documented zoonotic spillover risk and pandemic potential
Dual updates suggest evolving situation with new cases or geographic spread across reporting period
threats.action: Activate enhanced biosurveillance at human-animal interface; enforce strict PPE protocols for exposed workers; accelerate H5N1 vaccine candidate stockpiling; coordinate with USDA and national veterinary authorities on poultry surveillance

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued 23 April 2026 indicating active circulation in the Americas
BSL-3 select agent requiring high-containment precautions
Ongoing transmission requiring regional alert level maintenance
threats.action: Strengthen case detection and contact tracing; ensure JYNNEOS vaccine availability in affected countries; implement risk communication targeting high-risk populations; report to IHR mechanism

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 13 March 2026 indicating active yellow fever activity
BSL-3 select agent with high case fatality rate in unvaccinated individuals
Seasonal patterns and epizootic cycles suggest potential for human spillover events
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk populations; implement emergency vaccination campaigns in affected areas; enhance Aedes and Haemagogus mosquito surveillance; activate rapid diagnostic testing capacity

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update 18 February 2026 indicating significant dengue burden in the Americas
Historical patterns suggest early 2026 data may reflect elevated transmission following 2025 hyperendemic season
Multi-serotype circulation increases risk of severe dengue
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations; ensure clinical capacity for severe dengue management; promote community-based mosquito source reduction; monitor for serotype shifts that may increase hemorrhagic fever risk

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and Respiratory Viruses
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses; Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alert 27 April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
Prior alert January 2026 noted simultaneous influenza and RSV co-circulation
December 2025 alert documented end of Southern Hemisphere season and start of Northern Hemisphere 2025-26 season indicating year-round global burden
threats.action: Promote seasonal influenza vaccination campaigns for Southern Hemisphere; ensure antiviral stockpile adequacy; enhance ILI/SARI sentinel surveillance; monitor for novel reassortant strains

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two consecutive PAHO updates December 2025 and March 2026 suggest sustained or resurging transmission
Multi-wave reporting pattern indicates incomplete vaccination coverage or waning immunity
Infants and unvaccinated individuals at highest risk for severe outcomes
threats.action: Audit DTP/Tdap vaccination coverage rates by country; implement catch-up immunization campaigns; ensure neonatal cocooning strategies; investigate potential antimicrobial resistance in circulating strains

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 3 February 2026 indicating measles activity in the Americas
Americas region previously achieved elimination status making any resurgence a significant public health event
Importation risk from endemic regions combined with coverage gaps threatens elimination status
threats.action: Conduct rapid vaccination coverage assessments; implement outbreak response immunization where coverage gaps identified; enhance airport and border health screening; strengthen laboratory confirmation capacity

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 2025 indicating HPS cases in the Americas
High case fatality rate (approximately 35-40%) makes even limited case counts significant
Rodent reservoir activity may be influenced by environmental and climate conditions
threats.action: Enhance rodent control in endemic areas; educate at-risk populations on exposure prevention; ensure clinical recognition protocols at frontline facilities; strengthen laboratory diagnostic capacity for rapid confirmation

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents are actively circulating in the Americas Region as of the reporting period. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) is the highest-priority concern, with PAHO issuing epidemiological updates in both November 2025 and March 2026, indicating sustained zoonotic activity with pandemic spillover potential. Monkeypox virus (Mpox, MPXV) is also actively circulating, with a dedicated PAHO update in April 2026 confirming ongoing transmission in the Americas. Yellow Fever virus, also a BSL-3 pathogen, triggered a March 2026 PAHO alert indicating active cases. All three detections warrant enhanced biosafety measures, IHR notification compliance, and coordinated international response.
amrSignals: Pertussis resurgence with two consecutive PAHO alerts may indicate macrolide resistance or vaccine-escape variants in circulating Bordetella pertussis strains warranting molecular surveillance
GLP-1 receptor agonist misuse alert (February 2026) signals broader antimicrobial stewardship and pharmaceutical governance concerns in the Americas that could intersect with AMR drivers
Sustained Dengue transmission across multiple serotypes increases selective pressure that may complicate antiviral development pipelines
emergingPatterns: Dual H5N1 alerts (November 2025 and March 2026) suggest sustained or escalating zoonotic influenza activity at the human-animal interface in the Americas, with potential for accelerated spillover risk

Simultaneous co-circulation of multiple arboviruses (Dengue, Chikungunya, Yellow Fever) across the Americas indicates a hyperendemic vector-borne disease environment likely amplified by climate-driven Aedes aegypti range expansion

Back-to-back pertussis epidemiological updates over a three-month period suggest a resurgent multi-country outbreak potentially linked to vaccine coverage gaps or waning immunity post-COVID disruptions

The concurrent start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season (April 2026) alongside active H5N1 zoonotic circulation increases the theoretical risk of reassortment events between seasonal and avian influenza viruses
ECDC issuing five consecutive weekly threat reports (Weeks 16-20, 2026) indicates sustained elevated communicable disease activity across the EU/EEA warranting continuous monitoring
